name: Georgia

statute.readVia: Current wording read as the unchanged/struck text in the official HB 1022 Senate substitute (LC 63 0166S, legis.ga.gov) and the Georgia DPS summary https://dps.georgia.gov/node/127

windshield.strip: no material reducing light transmission on the windshield, except a transparent item, not red or amber, on the uppermost 6 inches
same as passenger cars (top 6 inches, not red or amber)

frontSide.note: windows to the right and left of the driver stay at 32% +/-3

tint.measuredHow: film + glass combined ('material and glazing ... when so applied')

medicalExemption.text: Department of Public Safety may issue an exemption on application supported by written attestation from a licensed physician or certified optometrist that the person must be shielded from the sun; covers vehicles owned by the person or in which they are a habitual passenger; conditions set by DPS.

penalty.text: Misdemeanor for operating with or installing illegal tint (§ 40-8-73.1(h)); general misdemeanor maximum fine $1,000 (O.C.G.A. § 17-10-3).

tint.lastAmended: 2005 (H.B. 20, effective May 2, 2005, per DPS); HB 1022 (2026) not enacted
quotes: reduce light transmission through the windshield or window to less than 32 percent, plus or minus 3 percent, or increase light reflectance to more than 20 percent
Any transparent item which is not red or amber in color which is placed on the uppermost six inches of the windshield
The rear windshield or the side or door windows, except those windows to the right and left of the driver of: (A) A multipurpose passenger vehicle
Any person who violates subsection (b) or (e) of this Code section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

handheldPhone.fineText: first conviction $50 and 1 point; second (within 24 months) $100 and 2 points; third+ $150 and 3 points (Governor's Office of Highway Safety)

radarDetector.note: commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

openQuestions: Georgia's official code (LexisNexis-hosted) is not readable by page; tint text read on 2026-10-24 in the official legis.ga.gov HB 1022 substitute (current wording shown with strike-outs) and the GA DPS page; phone fines on the Governor's Office of Highway Safety page.

HB 1022 (2026 session) would have set front side windows at 28% and rear windows at 15% and banned electric tinting; it passed the House (Feb 17, 2026) but its last action was Senate second reading (Mar 25, 2026) - treated as not enacted. Confirm on legis.ga.gov.
Windshield rule: the 6-inch top strip comes from the exception for transparent items not red/amber; DPS describes it as tint above the AS-1 line - the statute itself does not mention AS-1.
maxFineUsd 1000 comes from the general misdemeanor statute (§ 17-10-3), not read directly.
No underglow or lift-height rule found.
Helmet (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-315): not confirmed on an official page (earlier read on a non-official copy of the code); left null.
Studded tires (O.C.G.A. § 40-8-74): not confirmed on an official page; left null.
